content.text: Create, rebind, and retire purely instructive bindings to external MCP servers (ADR-0043) — they describe when and how an agent uses an external tool; they connect nothing.

Conventions: Load only the sections of the 'Agent-Building Conventions' resource this playbook needs — before writing, in one call: fetch_resource(resource_id, block_ids=["res-conv-h-exttool", "res-conv-h-status"]). A heading anchor returns its whole section; the resource_id is in this playbook's links (linked_blocks). Load other sections only when needed (anchors via list_resource_blocks).
Create external tool; maintain external tool; create tool binding; maintain tool binding; connect a tool; swap a tool; insert a tool-ref.

First identify the mode: Create, when a capability has no binding yet; Update/Rebind, when an existing binding is changed or the tool behind it is swapped; Retire, when a binding is taken out of service. ALWAYS read list_external_tools() or get_external_tool(alias) first — the alias resolves by either UUID OR capability alias.

Create — Understand: Clarify the CAPABILITY (what should the agent be able to do: manage to-dos, read appointments, ...), the concrete tool (product name), the MCP server name in the runtime, and the relevant tool identifiers. Choose the alias as a capability identifier, NOT as a product name ('todo' instead of 'todoist') — the alias is immutable after Create, but the product behind it stays swappable. Slug rules: alphanumeric/hyphen/underscore, 1-64 characters, workspace-unique (409 on collision).

Create — Write: create_external_tool(data) with name, alias, and content: display_name (the concrete tool's display name), mcp_server_name (connector name in the runtime), tool_names (relevant MCP tool identifiers), usage_notes (Markdown: when/how to use it, do's/don'ts), and fallback_note (behavior when the server is missing or not connected). This produces a draft version 1. Only set locale explicitly if the binding is meant to deliberately deviate from the workspace language — write usage_notes and fallback_note in that language (see the Language section in the Agent-Building Conventions).

Update/Rebind: update_external_tool(tool_id, data) — a PUT on an active version creates a new draft (409 as long as a draft is already open). Swapping the tool (e.g., Todoist → Things 3) means: swap the content, keep the alias — all tool-ref pills stay valid, not a single playbook/persona edit is needed. That's exactly what this aggregate exists for.

Use: Reference the binding in playbook, persona, resource, or template bodies via the tool-ref placeholder: the token {{tool-ref:<alias>}} in the Markdown text; the server turns it into a pill on save. It expands at fetch time to whichever binding is currently ACTIVE; without an active version it renders as an unresolved placeholder (miss). Check the usage notes + fallback beforehand via get_external_tool(alias).

Status: transition_external_tool(tool_id, version, to) follows draft→review→active→inactive. Only 'active' makes the binding visible for tool-ref expansion and agent reads (agents filter on status='active'). Promote/Retire (→active/→inactive) requires admin rights server-side, or promote_retire. restore_external_tool(tool_id, version) non-destructively restores an older version as a new draft.

Granting policy: If a domain agent should maintain bindings itself, set its tool_policy.external_tool_write=true via update_agent (is_within: you can only grant what you carry yourself). Read visibility is controlled by external_tool_read (all/none; 'assigned' falls back to 'all' — external tools are a flat workspace catalog with no assignment). When in doubt: domain agents only read, writing stays with the builder.

Using the product name as the alias ('todoist' instead of 'todo') — the alias won't meaningfully survive a tool swap. Wanting to change the alias afterward (it's immutable; if the alias is genuinely wrong: create a new binding, retire the old one, migrate the pills).

Storing server URLs, credentials, API keys, or other secrets in usage_notes/fallback_note — the binding is purely instructive (ADR-0043 tier B); connection data lives in the agent runtime, never in Who2Be.

Duplicating tool instructions as free text in playbooks/personas instead of setting a tool-ref pill (drift risk — exactly what this aggregate solves). Creating a NEW binding on a tool swap instead of rebinding (leaves orphaned pills and two competing aliases for one capability).

After writing, report: alias + display name, version status (draft/review/active), and the next step (review/activation — only promote yourself after explicit approval). Show where the binding is used or should be used (tool-ref pills), and whether domain agents need policy changes.
